actions.label: Provide food rations or compensation to guards and their families
Grant FWB unescorted free movement inside the camp
Assist FWB with distribution documentation and donor forms
Maintain perimeter security during distribution, including generator parts and fuel
Have guards organize and implement block-by-block food distribution
Allow FWB to hire vetted local assistants, prioritising local residents
Commit that FWB food will not be diverted and reaches all refugees
Conduct, scale back, or drop the donor-required nutritional assessment in favour of camp registration data
Coordinate public communications with the commander and refrain from publicity
Deliver food rations on an ongoing, scheduled long-term basis
Carry out distribution through existing camp guard structures
Distribute food equally to all registered refugees, including suspected groups

goals.label: Commander's personal safety and legal exposure
FWB and aid staff move freely and unescorted inside the camp
Food is distributed fairly to all refugees, including disfavoured or suspected groups
Camp guards and militia control food distribution
Camp power and infrastructure (generators, fuel, parts) keep running
Camp stability, free of riots, violence or perimeter breaches
Commander's authority over the camp is undermined
Control of the camp's narrative and information
FWB is seen as neutral and independent from armed actors
Food aid is diverted to guards or militia instead of refugees
Guards and their families are fed or compensated, keeping guards loyal
Host town economy and goodwill, with local actors prioritised
Refugees stay contained in the camp and do not reach the capital
Refugees' nutritional needs are reliably assessed
Safety of FWB staff and local assistants from threats or violence
The camp receives an ongoing, reliable food supply
Burden of FWB assessments, paperwork and procedures
Distribution is documented and meets donor accountability requirements
FWB sustains a long-term food aid program in the camp
Local hiring for the aid effort is chosen independently of camp authorities
Outsiders, including hostile actors, move freely inside the camp
Senior Militia Leader's trust and militia demands satisfied

redLines.label: Allow FWB staff and FWB-chosen assistants to manage food disbursement directly
redLines.quote: If FWB's hiring of local independent laborers for the food distribution goes ahead, there can be no trust in those people not to engage in the stirring of unrest and even potentially in support for hidden terrorists through the sharing of items or information.

redLines.label: Manage food disbursement through FWB staff and FWB-chosen local assistants
redLines.quote: If FWB's hiring of local independent laborers for the food distribution goes ahead, there can be no trust in those people not to engage in the stirring of unrest and even potentially in support for hidden terrorists through the sharing of items or information.

redLines.label: Provide food rations or compensation to guards and their families
redLines.quote: If they see the refugees eating better than they are, they may well rebel, and it may be your head. Or someone in your family's head.

assumptions: Commitments are binding and additive.
Goals and goal-action links were each extracted 3 times by a model; only those found in a majority of runs are kept.
Actions are chosen to bring about as much goal value as possible, within the solver's size limit.
Our values are the median of stances elicited from our role card.
The opponent column is the expected value of an elicited stance distribution (shared documents only); each opponent reading is one draw from it, independently per goal.
Stance labels map to numbers by a fixed scale (game.stance_values), not a measured utility.

Red lines and must-haves come from our role card, each with a verbatim quote. No plan may include a red-line action, leave out a must-have, or pass through a state worth less to us than our BATNA (the bottom line).
